children: European stocks opened the week higher, with the STOXX 50 gaining 0.8% and the STOXX 600 rising 0.6%, recovering some ground after a weak previous week.

Sentiment was supported by falling oil prices, as investors weighed resilient flows through the Middle East against escalating regional tensions, including attacks on Saudi Arabia, and a US claim that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an “energy ceasefire”.
Investors are also preparing for the start of earnings season, with ASML and LVMH set to report quarterly results this week.
Banking stocks led the gains, while utilities also advanced, whereas energy shares came under pressure.
HSBC rose 2.1%, Banco Santander gained 1.8%, BBVA added 1.6% and BNP Paribas climbed 1.0%.
Automakers Renault and Stellantis were among the top performers, advancing 3.1% and 2.5%, respectively.
Nordex jumped 3.8% after reporting a 30% year-on-year increase in project intake in the third quarter.

title: European Stocks Kick Off the Week Higher
